title: Security review - Encryption/KMS/BYOK/HSM - NovaFintech
summary: Redwood team walked NovaFintech through encryption at-rest and in-transit, KMS integrations, BYOK options and HSM support. Customer emphasized requirement for HSM-backed keys for production, auditability, and key rotation controls. Next steps: share KMS integration guide, HSM whitepaper, schedule BYOK PoC in Redwood Dedicated environment.
topics: Audit logs and key access tracing
next_steps: Redwood to share KMS integration guide and HSM whitepaper (Maya)
Schedule BYOK PoC in Dedicated environment (Evan + NovaFintech)
Customer to provide list of internal compliance questions for SOC2/ISO mapping
action_items: Maya Patel | Share KMS integration doc and HSM whitepaper | 2027-01-05
Evan Chen | Send pricing and scope for Dedicated BYOK PoC | 2026-12-29
Rajiv Malhotra | Provide internal key policy and required FIPS/HSM certs | 2027-01-08
notes: Customer is sensitive about control plane access and wants assurances that key material never leaves their HSM. They asked about Redwood logs and the ability to prove non-access to wrapped keys. Also asked about cross-region key replication and disaster recovery for KMS-backed keys.
transcript:
00:00:00 Evan Chen: hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll run through encryption and key mgmt today, maya my se will cover the technical bits.
00:00:07 Tom Brooks: yep thanks, we have Rajiv and Lina and Hannah here, looking forward.
00:00:12 Maya Patel: great, quick agenda: at-rest, in-transit, KMS integrations, BYOK, HSM, rotation, and logging. We'll keep it flexible.
00:00:23 Rajiv Malhotra: quick note - our bar is HSM backed keys for anything PII and payment tokens; we need proof of no-access and full audit logs.
00:00:32 Evan Chen: totally, understood. to set context, Redwood offers hosted and dedicated and private - hosted uses our managed KMS for convenience, dedicated can integrate customer KMS, and private gives you full control.
00:00:48 Lina Gomez: when you say integrate customer KMS, do you mean we can bring our AWS KMS keys? or GCP? what's the flow?
00:00:57 Maya Patel: yes both, we support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault. flow is typically envelope encryption: model artifacts and data at rest are encrypted with a data key that is wrapped by your KMS key. we never persist your plain data key unencrypted.
00:01:15 Tom Brooks: and for hosted - does Redwood ever hold unwrapped keys?
00:01:19 Maya Patel: in hosted mode we manage the wrapping key, so we hold wrapped keys; we don't have access to your plaintext wrapped data keys. for customers that need assurance, BYOK in Dedicated or Private is recommended.
00:01:35 Rajiv Malhotra: ok can you explain BYOK in dedicated - and HSM? we require FIPS 140-2 level 3 HSMs.
00:01:44 Evan Chen: sure. with Dedicated BYOK you provision a customer-managed CMK in your cloud KMS or external HSM. Redwood integrates via the KMS API to perform wrap/unwrap ops. if you want HSM-backed keys managed in your account, the KMS providers (AWS CloudHSM, Google HSM, Azure HSM) can satisfy FIPS level depending on config.
00:02:05 Lina Gomez: is there a need to export keys to Redwood? that's a hard no for us.
00:02:10 Maya Patel: no export is required. the wrapping/unwrapping happens as API calls to your KMS; Redwood never imports the raw key material. the data key is generated by our service but immediately wrapped by your CMK and only the wrapped form is stored.
00:02:25 Rajiv Malhotra: what about edge cases - like emergency recovery or rewrap? can Redwood initiate rewraps? who triggers rotation?
00:02:33 Maya Patel: rotation can be customer-triggered or automated. rewrap requests are performed through your KMS - Redwood can call the API when authorized; otherwise you can run the rewrap job. we recommend maintaining a key rotation policy in your KMS with least privilege roles.
00:02:48 Tom Brooks: we need strong audit traces showing which principal requested unwraps. do you surface those logs?
00:02:55 Maya Patel: yes, we log KMS API calls we make, and you will also have the cloud provider's KMS logs. for Dedicated and Private deployments you can centralize logs into your SIEM. our console surfaces a combined audit view but the raw KMS/Audit logs live with you in your cloud account when BYOK is used.
00:03:15 Hannah Lee: does Redwood maintain any long-term copy of unwrapped data for caching or inference? any chance of plaintext being written to disk?
00:03:24 Maya Patel: we use in-memory KV cache for model state; disk persistence is encrypted with data keys. plaintext is not persisted. for high-security customers we can configure memory pinning and zero-dump policies in Private deployments.
00:03:40 Rajiv Malhotra: memory pinning? can you elaborate?
00:03:44 Maya Patel: it's an option where the runtime avoids swapping and clears memory after use; it's part of our dedicated/private runtime config. not enabled by default on hosted.
00:03:54 Tom Brooks: cross-region replication - if we have keys in primary region, how do you handle DR?
00:03:59 Evan Chen: you can choose to replicate CMKs across regions using your cloud KMS replication features or keep keys separate and have regional CMKs. Redwood's routing can be configured to use region-specific wrapped keys for serving.
00:04:12 Lina Gomez: ok, what about HSM-backed external vendors? can we use an on-prem HSM that Redwood calls into?
00:04:19 Maya Patel: yes with Private deployments we support on-prem HSMs or customer-managed networked HSMs. that requires network peering/VPN and appropriate firewall rules. Redwood's control plane can be configured to not see key operations if you host the KMS in your VPC and only the data plane has access.
00:04:36 Rajiv Malhotra: control plane - does Redwood have any admin ability to unwrap in emergency?
00:04:41 Evan Chen: by default, no. for Hosted customers we have escalation paths that involve keys in our managed KMS and legal processes. For Dedicated/BYOK in customer-managed KMS, Redwood does not hold unwrapped key material and cannot unwrap without your KMS granting permission. any emergency access would be through your IAM policies.
00:05:00 Tom Brooks: we need to be sure about certificate chains and attestation - like you said HSMs, do you provide attestation docs?
00:05:07 Maya Patel: we can supply HSM whitepapers and sample attestation outputs; for cloud HSMs you get provider attestation (cloud provider). for on-prem we can work with your security team to capture attestation evidence.
00:05:20 Rajiv Malhotra: log retention - we must keep key access logs for 7 years for audit. is that possible?
00:05:26 Evan Chen: log retention is handled on your KMS/Cloud Logging side when BYOK is used, so yes you can configure retention for as long as needed. Redwood's console also retains combined traces depending on plan but regulator retention should be on your side.
00:05:40 Lina Gomez: any limitations for model checkpoint encryption or KV caches? size limits, throughput issues?
00:05:45 Maya Patel: performance is generally unaffected because wrapping/unwrapping is only for data keys. we cache unwrapped data keys in-memory for short periods to avoid per-request latencies; the wrap/unwrap ops happen primarily at checkpoint save/load or rotation. if you want a pure no-expose policy we can shorten cache lifetimes.
00:06:05 Rajiv Malhotra: what's your recommendation for tokenization - do you encrypt token store separately?
00:06:09 Maya Patel: treat token store as a separate data domain and use separate data keys with RBAC. we recommend different CMKs per environment or data sensitivity tier.
00:06:20 Tom Brooks: competitors - BigCloudAI said they can do HSM but they require key escrow, is that common?
00:06:26 Evan Chen: every vendor differs; Redwood's stance is no-key-escrow for BYOK in customer-managed KMS. if you need escrow, that's a legal agreement outside of default ops.
00:06:39 Rajiv Malhotra: auditability - we want to map actions to Redwood principals in our audit. how do you map API calls to service identities?
00:06:47 Maya Patel: we use distinct service principals per deployment and tag logs with instance IDs; when integrated with your IAM we can map calls to roles and provide trace correlation IDs.
00:06:59 Lina Gomez: sample artifacts please - we want to review the integration guide and a network diagram.
00:07:05 Evan Chen: we'll share the KMS integration guide, HSM whitepaper, and a sample network diagram. I'll drop links after the call.
00:07:12 Rajiv Malhotra: one more - can you support Hardware Security Module in a self-hosted HSM that uses PKCS#11?
00:07:18 Maya Patel: yes, our Private runtime supports PKCS#11 HSMs; we have connectors for common vendors. it requires some config and testing but it's supported.
00:07:29 Tom Brooks: any compatibility matrix? like which cloud regions and HSM families?
00:07:33 Maya Patel: yes we'll send the compatibility matrix; generally AWS CloudHSM, AWS KMS HSM, Google Cloud HSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and common PKCS#11 appliances are covered.
00:07:45 Rajiv Malhotra: we need contractual language for key ownership and non-access.
00:07:49 Evan Chen: understood - legal can provide a BYOK addendum and SCB clauses, we'll loop in your counsel.
00:07:55 Hannah Lee: SOC2 and ISO mapping - will you provide control mappings for encryption controls?
00:08:00 Maya Patel: yes, we have SOC2 and ISO artifacts and control mappings specifically for key mgmt and encryption, we'll share the redacted reports and a control matrix.
00:08:10 Lina Gomez: ok let's recap next steps.
00:08:13 Evan Chen: recap: Redwood to share KMS integration guide, HSM whitepaper, compatibility matrix, sample network diagram, and BYOK PoC plan. NovaFintech to provide key policy and compliance questions. we'll meet again to kick off the PoC.
00:08:27 Rajiv Malhotra: perfect, thanks.
00:08:29 Evan Chen: thanks all, end.
